curriculum.lesson_evidence: Props and costumes can be made from recycled materials such as cardboard, paper, fabric scraps and string. A design plan shows what the item is, which materials it uses and how it will be made. Keep props light and soft with no sharp points, and never use things that can hurt others. Use scissors carefully, tape securely and ask an adult for help with anything tricky. A good costume piece is simple and shows a key trait of the character, like a gold crown for a king or a feather for a bird.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Design a simple crown for a character who is generous and kind. List the materials, one safety choice and one decoration that shows the trait.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Cardboard band with rounded gold paper points and a paper heart in the middle to show kindness. Materials: cardboard, gold paper, glue and tape. Safety: round points, not sharp.' The decoration is linked to the character trait.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that a costume has to be very detailed or bought from a shop. Simple recycled materials can show a character just as well, as long as it is safe and easy to move in.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a prop and a costume piece for a character using recycled materials. Draw a design plan first with materials and safety choices. Wear them in a short scene and write one improvement. Ask an adult to help with scissors and glue.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teaching.feedback: The new example should use the same arts idea as the model, but with different content or material.
teaching.fix: Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
teaching.guided_attempt: Make or describe one fresh example that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your main choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Props and costumes can be made from recycled materials such as cardboard, paper, fabric scraps and string. A design plan shows what the item is, which materials it uses and how it will be made. Keep props light and soft with no sharp points, and never use things that can hurt others. Use scissors carefully, tape securely and ask an adult for help with anything tricky. A good costume piece is simple and shows a key trait of the character, like a gold crown for a king or a feather for a bird. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
